title.zh: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋
title.en: Volume 391 Biographies 178: Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong
title.raw: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋

sentences.zh: 倭仁，字艮峰，烏齊格里氏，蒙古正紅旗人，河南駐防。

translations.literal: Wo Ren, whose style name was Genfeng, was of the Uqigeri clan, a Mongol of the Plain Red Banner, and was stationed on garrison duty at Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren, style name Genfeng, belonged to the Uqigeri clan. A Mongol of the Plain Red Banner, he was posted on garrison duty in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Daoguang reign he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in the ninth year of Daoguang (1829), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 歷中允、侍講、侍讀、庶子、侍講學士、侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as middle attendant, expositor, reader, household tutor of the heir apparent, expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of middle attendant, expositor, reader, household tutor of the heir apparent, and expositor and reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of his reign (1842), he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to be president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「行政莫先於用人，用人莫先於君子小人之辨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Wo Ren responded to the imperial edict calling for memorials and stated in summary: 'In administration nothing comes before employing men; in employing men nothing comes before distinguishing gentlemen from petty men.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, Wo Ren answered the edict inviting memorials. In substance he wrote: 'In governing, nothing precedes the choice of personnel; in choosing personnel, nothing precedes telling the gentleman from the petty man.'

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人藏於心術者難知，發於事蹟者易見。

translations.literal: As for gentlemen and petty men, what is hidden in the mind is hard to know, but what appears in deeds is easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: What lies hidden in the heart is hard to discern; what shows in conduct is easy to see.

sentences.zh: 大抵君子訥拙，小人佞巧；

translations.literal: Generally, the gentleman is slow of speech and awkward, the petty man flattering and clever;
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, the gentleman is plain-spoken and unadorned, the petty man glib and artful;

sentences.zh: 君子澹定，小人躁競；

translations.literal: the gentleman calm and settled, the petty man restless and contentious;
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman composed and steady, the petty man restless and grasping;

sentences.zh: 君子愛惜人才，小人排擠異類；

translations.literal: the gentleman cherishes talent, the petty man drives out those unlike himself;
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman values talent, the petty man squeezes out the unlike-minded;

sentences.zh: 君子圖遠大，以國家元氣為先，小人計目前，以聚斂刻薄為務。

translations.literal: the gentleman plans for what is far-reaching and puts the nation's vital energy first, the petty man calculates for the present moment and makes harsh exaction his business.
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman looks to the long term and puts the state's underlying strength first, while the petty man counts only the present and makes harsh levies his trade.

sentences.zh: 剛正不撓、無所阿鄉者，君子也；

translations.literal: He who is upright and unyielding and curries favor with no one is a gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Upright, unbending, and beholden to no faction—that is the gentleman;

sentences.zh: 依違兩可、工於趨避者，小人也。

translations.literal: he who wavers between two sides and is skilled at evasion is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: equivocal, skilled at sidestepping—that is the petty man.

sentences.zh: 諫諍匡弼、進憂危之議，動人主之警心者，君子也；

translations.literal: He who remonstrates and assists, who advances words of peril and warning to stir the ruler's vigilance, is a gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: He who remonstrates and steadies the throne, who offers warnings of peril to rouse the sovereign—that is the gentleman;

sentences.zh: 喜言氣數、不畏天變，長人君之逸志者，小人也。

translations.literal: he who delights in speaking of fate and omens, who does not fear heavenly changes, and who fosters the ruler's inclination to ease is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: He who talks of fate, shrugs at heaven's warnings, and indulges the ruler's wish for ease—that is the petty man.

sentences.zh: 公私邪正，相反如此。

translations.literal: Public and private, straight and crooked—thus opposite are they.
translations.idiomatic: In public duty and private motive, in rectitude and depravity, they stand thus opposed.

sentences.zh: 皇上天亶聰明，孰賢孰否，必能洞知。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is endowed by Heaven with keen intelligence; who is worthy and who is not, you must surely perceive through and through.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Heaven-given discernment surely penetrates who is worthy and who is not.

sentences.zh: 第恐一人之心思耳目，揣摩者眾，混淆者多，幾微莫辨，情偽滋紛，愛憎稍涉偏私，取捨必至失當。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that with one man's thoughts, ears, and eyes, those who fathom his wishes are many and those who confuse him are many; what is subtle cannot be distinguished, truth and falsehood grow tangled, if love and hate touch even slightly on partiality, choice and rejection will necessarily go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that a single mind and pair of ears, courted by so many who read its wishes, can be clouded by so many voices that the subtle is lost, truth and pretense tangle, a trace of favor skews judgment, and appointments go awry.

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，豈有他術，在皇上好學勤求，使聖志益明，聖德日固而已。

translations.literal: To know men is to be wise—what other art is there? It lies only in Your Majesty's love of learning and diligent seeking, so that the sage resolve grows ever clearer and sage virtue is daily strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: 'To know men is wisdom'—there is no other method than Your Majesty's own love of learning and earnest inquiry, by which the imperial mind grows clearer and imperial virtue firmer day by day.

sentences.zh: 宋程顥雲，'古者人君必有誦訓箴諫之臣'。

translations.literal: Song dynasty Cheng Hao said, 'In antiquity every ruler had ministers who recited instruction and offered admonition.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao of the Song said, 'In antiquity every ruler had ministers to recite lessons and offer remonstrance.'

sentences.zh: 請命老成之儒，講論道義，又擇天下賢俊，陪侍法從。

translations.literal: I beg that seasoned Confucians be ordered to expound the Way and its moral principles, and that worthy men of the realm be chosen to attend in the entourage of the law.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that venerable scholars be charged to expound the Way and its moral teaching, and that the finest talent of the realm be chosen to attend Your Majesty in study.

sentences.zh: 我朝康熙間，熊賜履上疏，亦以'延訪真儒'為說。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's Kangxi reign, Xiong Cilü submitted a memorial likewise urging 'to extend invitation to true Confucians.'
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign of our dynasty, Xiong Cilü likewise memorialized urging the court to 'seek out true Confucians.'

sentences.zh: 二臣所言，皆修養身心之要，用人行政之源也。

translations.literal: What these two ministers spoke of are all essentials for cultivating body and mind, and the source of employing men and administering government.
translations.idiomatic: What both ministers urged goes to the root of self-cultivation and to the source of sound appointment and governance.

sentences.zh: 天下治亂系宰相，君德成就責講筵。

translations.literal: Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends on the chief minister; the achievement of the ruler's virtue rests on the lecture seat.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder in the realm hinge on the chief minister; the maturing of the ruler's virtue rests on his teachers at the lecture seat.

sentences.zh: 惟君德成就而後輔弼得人，輔弼得人而後天下可治。

translations.literal: Only when the ruler's virtue is achieved can the right assistants be obtained; only when the right assistants are obtained can the realm be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the ruler's virtue is formed can worthy assistants be found; only then can the realm be brought to order.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上稱其切直，因諭大小臣工進言以倭仁為法。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it as incisive and forthright, and thereupon instructed officials great and small to take Wo Ren as their model in offering counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor praised its blunt honesty and told officials at every level to take Wo Ren as their model in speaking up.

sentences.zh: 未幾，禮部侍郎曾國籓奏用人三策，上复憶倭仁言，手詔同褒勉焉。

translations.literal: Before long, Zeng Guofan, vice president of the Ministry of Rites, memorialized three policies for employing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's words and issued a handwritten edict commending both alike.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Zeng Guofan of the Ministry of Rites submitted three policies on appointments. The Emperor recalled Wo Ren's memorial as well and issued a personal edict praising both men together.

sentences.zh: 尋予副都統銜，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given the brevet rank of vice commander-in-chief and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the brevet rank of vice commander-in-chief and sent as assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 大理寺少卿田雨公疏言倭仁用違其才，上曰：「邊疆要任，非投閒置散也。

translations.literal: Tian Yugong, vice president of the Court of Judicial Review, memorialized that Wo Ren's appointment misused his talents. The Emperor said: 'A frontier post of importance is not idling someone in neglect.'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yugong, vice president of the Court of Judicial Review, argued that Wo Ren had been misassigned. The Emperor replied: 'A key frontier post is not banishment to idleness.'

sentences.zh: 若以外任皆左遷，豈國家文武兼資、內外並重之意乎？

translations.literal: If every outside appointment were treated as a demotion, how would that accord with the state's intent to employ both civil and military talent and to value inner and outer service equally?
translations.idiomatic: If every provincial posting were treated as a demotion, how would that match the state's aim to use civil and military talent alike and to weigh inner and outer service equally?

sentences.zh: 」咸豐二年，倭仁复上敬陳治本一疏，上謂其意在責難陳善，尚無不合，惟僅泛語治道，因戒以留心邊務，勿託空言。

translations.literal: ' In the second year of Xianfeng, Wo Ren again submitted a respectful memorial on fundamental remedies. The Emperor said its intent to hold him to account while offering good counsel was not improper, but that it spoke only in generalities about governing the Way, and therefore admonished him to attend to frontier affairs and not trust to empty words.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the second year of Xianfeng (1852), Wo Ren again submitted a memorial on fundamental remedies. The Emperor allowed that its intent—to admonish while offering sound counsel—was acceptable, but said it spoke only in generalities about governance, and warned him to mind frontier duties rather than offer empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 候補道何桂珍上封事，言倭仁秉性忠貞，見理明決，生平言行不負所學，請任以艱鉅，未許。

translations.literal: He Guizhen, an expectant circuit intendant, submitted a sealed memorial saying Wo Ren's nature was loyal and upright, his grasp of principle clear and decisive, and that in life his words and deeds did not betray his learning; he asked that Wo Ren be entrusted with arduous tasks. This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He Guizhen, an expectant circuit intendant, submitted a sealed memorial praising Wo Ren's loyalty, clarity of judgment, and conduct true to his learning, and asking that he be given heavy responsibility. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年，倭仁劾葉爾羌回部郡王阿奇木伯克愛瑪特攤派路費及護衛索贓等罪，詔斥未經確訊，率行參奏，下部議，降三級調用。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wo Ren impeached Emirat, the Hui beg of Yarkand, for levying travel expenses and for his guards demanding bribes, among other crimes. An edict rebuked him for memorializing without thorough investigation and referred the case to the ministries for deliberation; he was demoted three ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1853) he impeached Emirat, the Muslim beg of Yarkand, for extorting travel fees and bribes from his guards, among other offenses. The court rebuked him for accusing without full inquiry; after ministry review he was demoted three ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 四年，侍郎王茂廕等請命會同籌辦京師團練，上以軍務非所長，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Vice President Wang Maoyin and others asked that Wo Ren be ordered jointly to organize capital militia training; the Emperor, holding that military affairs were not his strength, shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wang Maoyin and others asked that Wo Ren help organize militia training around the capital. The Emperor, judging military affairs not his forte, set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 尋命以侍講候補入直上書房，授惇郡王讀。

translations.literal: Shortly he was ordered, as an expectant expositor, to enter service in the Imperial Study and to instruct the Prince of Dun in reading.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed, while still an expectant expositor, to the Imperial Study as tutor to the Prince of Dun.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺卿、盛京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice president of the Ministry of Rites at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and as vice president of the Ministry of Rites at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 七年，調戶部，管奉天府尹事，劾罷盛京副都統增慶、兵部侍郎富呢雅杭阿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and supervised the affairs of the prefect of Fengtian; he impeached and secured the dismissal of Zengqing, vice commander-in-chief at Mukden, and Funiyihang'a, vice president of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he moved to the Ministry of Revenue, oversaw the Fengtian prefecture, and impeached Zengqing, Mukden's vice commander-in-chief, and Funiyihang'a, vice president of the Ministry of War, securing their removal.

sentences.zh: 及頒詔中外，命充朝鮮正使。

translations.literal: When an edict was promulgated within and without, he was ordered to serve as chief envoy to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: When a major edict was issued to the realm, he was appointed chief envoy to Korea.

sentences.zh: 召回京，授都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was appointed left censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Beijing, he was made left censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862) he was promoted to minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 兩宮皇太后以倭仁老成端謹，學問優長，命授穆宗讀。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers, because Wo Ren was mature, upright, and careful and excelled in learning, ordered him to instruct Emperor Muzong in reading.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers, finding Wo Ren seasoned, upright, and learned, appointed him tutor to Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 倭仁輯古帝王事蹟，及古今名臣奏議，附說進之，賜名啟心金鑑，置弘德殿資講肄。

translations.literal: Wo Ren compiled deeds of ancient emperors and kings and memorials of famous ministers past and present, added explanations, and presented them; they were granted the title Mirror of the Heart to Open the Mind and placed in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for use in lectures and study.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren compiled deeds of ancient rulers and selected memorials of eminent ministers, annotated them, and presented the collection. It was named Mirror of the Heart to Open the Mind and kept in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for the emperor's instruction.

sentences.zh: 倭仁素嚴正，穆宗尤敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Wo Ren had always been stern and upright, and Emperor Muzong especially revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren was known for his severity and rectitude, and the young emperor especially revered and stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，調工部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, transferred to minister of Works, and appointed associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the chancellorship of the Hanlin, retained the Ministry of Works, and was named associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「河南自咸豐三年以後，粵、捻焚掠，蓋藏已空，州縣誅求仍復無厭。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: 'Since the third year of Xianfeng in Henan, the Cantonese and Nian rebels have burned and plundered until storehouses are empty, yet the prefectures and districts still extort without end.'
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: 'Since the third year of Xianfeng, Henan has been ravaged by Taiping and Nian bandits until granaries are bare, yet county and prefectural officials still squeeze the people without surcease.'

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能盡擇州縣，則必慎擇督撫。

translations.literal: If the court cannot choose every prefecture and district, it must carefully choose governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: If the court cannot vet every local magistrate, it must at least choose governors-general and governors with care.

sentences.zh: 督撫不取之屬員，則屬員自無可挾以為恣睢之地。

translations.literal: If governors-general and governors do not take bribes from their subordinates, then subordinates naturally have nothing to rely on as a place for arbitrary tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: When governors do not profit from their staffs, subordinates have no leverage for arbitrary rule.

sentences.zh: 今日河南積習，祗曰民刁詐，不曰官貪庸；

translations.literal: Today's entrenched habit in Henan is only to call the people crafty and deceitful, not to call officials greedy and incompetent;
translations.idiomatic: The entrenched habit in Henan today is to blame only the people's cunning, never official greed or incompetence;

sentences.zh: 祗狃於愚民之抗官，不思所以致抗之由。

translations.literal: only to cling to the notion of ignorant commoners resisting officials, without thinking of what causes such resistance.
translations.idiomatic: only to fixate on ignorant peasants defying magistrates, without asking what drives such defiance.

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷慎察大吏，力挽積習，寇亂之源，庶幾可弭。

translations.literal: It lies only in the court's careful scrutiny of high officials and strenuous reversal of entrenched habits—then perhaps the source of bandit turmoil can be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Only if the court scrutinizes its senior appointees and forcefully reverses these habits can the roots of rebellion perhaps be cut.

sentences.zh: 」是年秋，拜文淵閣大學士，疏劾新授廣東巡撫黃贊湯貪詐，解其職。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity; he memorialized impeaching the newly appointed governor of Guangdong, Huang Zantang, for greed and deceit, and had him removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he entered the Grand Secretariat. He impeached the newly appointed governor of Guangdong, Huang Zantang, for corruption and fraud, and secured his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 六年，同文館議考選正途五品以下京外官入館肄習天文算學，聘西人為教習。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Tongwen Guan proposed selecting regular-route officials of the fifth rank and below from the capital and provinces to study astronomy and mathematics in the academy, and hiring Westerners as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1867) the Tongwen Guan proposed enrolling regular-route officials of the fifth rank and below from Beijing and the provinces to study astronomy and mathematics, with Westerners as instructors.

sentences.zh: 倭仁謂根本之圖，在人心不在技藝，尤以西人教習為不可；

translations.literal: Wo Ren said the fundamental plan lay in men's hearts, not in technical skills, and especially that Western instructors were unacceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren argued that the fundamental remedy lay in men's hearts, not in technical skill, and above all that Western teachers were unacceptable;

sentences.zh: 且謂必習天文算學，應求中國能精其法者，上疏請罷議。

translations.literal: and he said that if astronomy and mathematics must be studied, Chinese who master their methods should be sought; he submitted a memorial asking that the proposal be dropped.
translations.idiomatic: and that if such studies were needed, Chinese masters of the methods should be found. He memorialized to halt the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是詔倭仁保薦，別設一館，即由倭仁督率講求。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Wo Ren to recommend men and to set up a separate academy, which Wo Ren himself was to supervise in study.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Wo Ren to nominate instructors and open a separate academy under his supervision.

sentences.zh: 復奏意中並無其人，不敢妄保。

translations.literal: He memorialized again that he had no such person in mind and dared not recommend rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He replied that he knew no one fit for the task and dared not recommend blindly.

sentences.zh: 尋命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: Shortly he was ordered to serve at the Yamen for the Management of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 倭仁屢疏懇辭，不允；

translations.literal: Wo Ren repeatedly memorialized earnestly declining; this was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren repeatedly begged to be excused, without success;

sentences.zh: 因稱疾篤，乞休，命解兼職，仍在弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: thereupon, claiming his illness was severe, he begged retirement; he was ordered to relinquish his additional posts but still to attend at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he then pleaded grave illness and asked to retire. The court relieved him of his extra posts but kept him at the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言大婚典禮宜崇節儉，及武英殿災，复偕徐桐、翁同龢疏請勤修聖德，停罷一切工程，以弭災變，並嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized that the grand wedding ceremonies should uphold frugality; when the Hall of Military Glory burned, he again joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in memorializing to urge diligent cultivation of sage virtue and the halting of all construction projects to quell heavenly calamities—and all was graciously accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he urged frugality for the imperial wedding. After fire destroyed the Hall of Military Glory, he joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in asking the emperor to cultivate virtue and halt all construction to appease heaven's warnings. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉文華殿大學士，以疾再乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was advanced to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and again begged retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and again asked to retire on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Guardian, entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and granted the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. Posthumously he was made Grand Guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，河南巡撫李鶴年奏建專祠於開封，允之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu, Li Henian, governor of Henan, memorialized to build a dedicated shrine at Kaifeng; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Guangxu (1882), Governor Li Henian of Henan memorialized for a private shrine at Kaifeng, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，曾國籓官京師，與倭仁、李棠階、吳廷棟、何桂珍、竇垿講求宋儒之學。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zeng Guofan held office in the capital, he together with Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan pursued the learning of Song Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zeng Guofan served in Beijing, he studied Song Neo-Confucianism together with Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan.

sentences.zh: 其後國籓出平大難，為中興名臣冠；

translations.literal: Afterward Guofan went out to quell great calamities and stood at the head of the renowned ministers of restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Guofan later went forth to quell the great rebellions and became the foremost statesman of the restoration;

sentences.zh: 倭仁作帝師，正色不阿；

translations.literal: Wo Ren served as the emperor's teacher, stern in countenance and yielding to none;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren served as imperial tutor, unbending in manner;

sentences.zh: 棠階、廷棟亦卓然有以自見焉。

translations.literal: Tangjie and Tingdong likewise distinguished themselves in their own right.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie and Tingdong likewise made names for themselves in their own spheres.

sentences.zh: 倭仁著有遺書十三卷。

translations.literal: Wo Ren left posthumous writings in thirteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren left collected writings in thirteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子福咸，江蘇鹽法道，署安徽徽寧池太廣道，咸豐十年，殉難寧國，贈太僕寺卿，騎都尉世職；

translations.literal: His son Fuxian was intendant of salt affairs in Jiangsu and acting intendant of the Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping-Guangde circuit in Anhui; in the tenth year of Xianfeng he died a martyr's death at Ningguo and was posthumously given the post of vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud and a hereditary captaincy of cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuxian served as Jiangsu salt intendant and acting Anhui circuit intendant; in the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860) he died defending Ningguo and was posthumously made vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud with a hereditary captaincy;

sentences.zh: 福裕，奉天府府尹。

translations.literal: Fuyu was prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu became prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 從子福潤，安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: His nephew Furun was governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Furun rose to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，外國兵入京師，闔家死焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, when foreign troops entered the capital, the whole family perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu (1900), when foreign troops entered Beijing, the entire family perished.

sentences.zh: 李棠階，字文園，河南河內人。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie, whose style name was Wenyuan, was a native of Henei in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie, style name Wenyuan, was from Henei in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the second year of Daoguang (1822), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 五遷至侍讀。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of reader.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became a Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，督廣東學政，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted to vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1842) he served as Guangdong education commissioner and was promoted to vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫黃恩彤奏請予鄉試年老武生職銜，嚴旨責譴，棠階亦因違例送考，議降三級調用，遂引疾家居。

translations.literal: When Governor Huang Entong memorialized to grant brevet titles to elderly military licentiates at the provincial examination, a stern edict rebuked him; Tangjie too, for irregularly sending candidates to the examination, was under deliberation to be demoted three ranks and transferred, and thereupon pleaded illness and remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Huang Entong asked to grant honorary titles to elderly military licentiates at the provincial exams, the court rebuked him sharply. Tangjie was also faulted for irregularly submitting candidates; after review he was to be demoted three ranks, and he retired home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，复日講，曾國籓薦棠階醇正堪備講官，召來京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, daily lectures were resumed; Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as pure and upright and fit to serve as lecturer, and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, daily lectures resumed. Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as upright and fit for the lecture seat, and he was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既而日講中輟，棠階以病未赴。

translations.literal: Before long the daily lectures ceased; Tangjie, on grounds of illness, did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: The lectures soon lapsed again, and Tangjie, pleading illness, did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，河北土寇蜂起，用尚書周祖培薦，命治河北團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, as Cantonese rebels invaded northward and local bandits in Hebei swarmed up, on the recommendation of Minister Zhou Zupei he was ordered to manage militia training in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng (1853), as Taiping forces pushed north and Hebei bandits rose everywhere, on Zhou Zupei's recommendation he was ordered to organize militia in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 棠階聯絡村鎮，名曰「友助社」。

translations.literal: Tangjie linked villages and market towns under the name 'Society of Mutual Aid.'
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie linked villages and towns into units he called the Society of Mutual Aid.

sentences.zh: 賊踞溫縣東河灘柳林，四出焚掠，棠階督團練擊之，村民未習戰，且無火器，殺賊數十人，卒不敵。

translations.literal: Bandits occupied the willow groves on the east river beach of Wen County and raided in all directions; Tangjie led the militia against them. The villagers were unused to fighting and had no firearms; they killed several dozen bandits but in the end could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits held the willow groves on Wen County's east river beach and raided widely. Tangjie led the militia against them, but the peasants were untrained and unarmed; though they killed dozens of bandits, they could not hold.

sentences.zh: 會山東巡撫李僡率兵至，賊引去。

translations.literal: When Li Xin, governor of Shandong, led troops there, the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong Governor Li Xin arrived with troops, the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊自渡黃河，始知民間有備，稍稍牽綴。

translations.literal: After the bandits themselves crossed the Yellow River, they came to know that the populace was prepared and were somewhat held back.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bandits crossed the Yellow River themselves, they found the countryside prepared and their advance slowed.

sentences.zh: 洎河北肅清，敘勞，加四品卿銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Hebei was pacified, his merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of fourth-rank grand secretary and awarded a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was cleared, his service was rewarded with a brevet fourth-rank grand secretary title and a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，詔起用舊臣，棠階應召至。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict recalled former officials to service; Tangjie answered the summons and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862) an edict recalled veteran officials; Tangjie answered and came to court.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「用人行政，惟在治心。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: 'In employing men and administering government, all lies in governing the heart.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Appointments and governance depend entirely on governing the heart.'

sentences.zh: 治心之要，莫先克己。

translations.literal: The essential of governing the heart is nothing before self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The key to governing the heart is self-restraint above all.

sentences.zh: 請於師保匡弼之馀，豫杜左右近習之漸。

translations.literal: I beg that beyond the tutors who assist and correct, the gradual encroachment of those close at hand be forestalled in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the tutors who guide and correct him, I ask that the emperor guard early against the gradual influence of those nearest his person.

sentences.zh: 暇時進講通鑑、大學衍義諸書，以收物格意誠之效。

translations.literal: In leisure hours advance lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and such books, to achieve the effect of investigating things and making the will sincere.
translations.idiomatic: In spare hours let him study the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and similar works, to achieve the discipline of investigating things and making the will sincere.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「紀綱之飭，在於嚴明賞罰。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The tightening of discipline lies in making rewards and punishments strict and clear.'
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'To restore discipline, rewards and punishments must be strict and clear.'

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷通諭諸事，務飭疆臣實力奉行，庶中外情志可通，而禍亂可弭。

translations.literal: In all matters of general notification from the court, frontier officials must be ordered to carry them out in earnest, so that sentiment within and without may communicate and calamity and turmoil may be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Every order from the court must be enforced in earnest by provincial officials, so that court and provinces may align and rebellion be checked.

sentences.zh: 」兩宮嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers graciously accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers approved his counsel.

sentences.zh: 授大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 先是兩江總督何桂清僨事逮治，部讞從重擬斬決，廷臣有右之者，言部臣有意畸重，仍從本律監候。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Guiqing, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, had been arrested for losing his post; the ministries' verdict proposed execution by decapitation with aggravation. Some court ministers supported him, saying the ministries had intentionally weighed the penalty too heavily, and the sentence reverted to imprisonment awaiting execution under the basic statute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, He Guiqing, governor-general of Jiangnan, had been arrested for abandoning his post. The ministries recommended aggravated decapitation, but some courtiers defended him, arguing the ministries had skewed the penalty; the sentence was reduced to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 棠階疏謂桂清貽誤封疆罪大，不當輕比，非公論。

translations.literal: Tangjie memorialized that Guiqing's crime of bringing disaster on the frontier was grave and should not be lightly compared—this was not public justice.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie memorialized that He Guiqing's crime of abandoning the frontier was grave and should not be lightly punished; to do so was not justice.

sentences.zh: 後桂清卒伏法。

translations.literal: Later Guiqing in the end suffered the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing was eventually executed.

sentences.zh: 連擢禮部侍郎、左都御史，署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice president of the Ministry of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and acting minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in quick succession to vice president of Rites, left censor-in-chief, and acting minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 召對，言：「治天下惟在安民，安民必先察吏。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he said: 'To govern the realm lies only in securing the people; to secure the people one must first scrutinize officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he said: 'Governing the realm depends on securing the people; securing the people begins with scrutinizing officials.'

sentences.zh: 今日之盜賊，即昔日之良民，皆地方有司貪虐激之成變。

translations.literal: Today's bandits are yesterday's good commoners—all provoked into rebellion by the greed and cruelty of local officials.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits of today were yesterday's law-abiding people, driven to revolt by greedy and abusive local officials.

sentences.zh: 為今日平亂計，非輕徭薄賦不能治本。

translations.literal: For today's plan to pacify disorder, without lightening corvée and reducing taxes one cannot remedy the root.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify disorder today, lighter burdens and lower taxes are the only way to reach the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 然非擇大吏，則守令不得其人，亦終不能收令行禁止之效。

translations.literal: Yet unless great officials are chosen, prefects and magistrates will not be the right men, and in the end one cannot achieve the effect of orders issued and prohibitions obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: But without choosing the right senior appointees, local magistrates will remain unfit, and orders will never truly be enforced.

sentences.zh: 」因極言河南亂事，及諸行省利病甚悉。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he spoke at length on the disorders in Henan and on the advantages and harms of the various provinces in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He went on at length about Henan's turmoil and the strengths and weaknesses of the provinces.

sentences.zh: 命為軍機大臣，具疏力辭，弗許。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Grand Councilor; he memorialized earnestly declining, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was named to the Grand Council but memorialized repeatedly to decline; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二年，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧克復，論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangning was recovered, his merit was recorded and he was given the brevet title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after Jiangning was recovered, he was rewarded with the brevet title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大憝既平，上諭中外臣工以兢業交勉。

translations.literal: Once the great enemy was pacified, the Emperor instructed officials within and without to encourage one another in diligence.
translations.idiomatic: After the great rebels were crushed, the Emperor urged officials throughout the realm to rededicate themselves to diligent service.

sentences.zh: 棠階語恭親王及同直諸大臣，謂當設誠致行，久而不懈，勿徒以空言相文飾，王深然之。

translations.literal: Tangjie spoke to Prince Gong and the other ministers on duty, saying they should set sincerity and carry it into action, long and without slackening, and not merely ornament one another with empty words; the prince deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie told Prince Gong and his colleagues on the Grand Council that they must act with sincere purpose and persevere, not trade empty phrases; the prince strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 翼日召對，王反复陳君臣交儆之義，棠階與同僚繼言之，兩宮改容嘉納。

translations.literal: The next day, summoned for audience, the prince repeatedly set forth the meaning of mutual vigilance between ruler and minister; Tangjie and his colleagues followed, and the two empress dowagers changed expression and graciously accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At the next audience the prince expounded mutual vigilance between ruler and ministers; Tangjie and others echoed him, and the empress dowagers visibly approved.

sentences.zh: 尋調禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太后命南書房、上書房諸臣纂輯前史事蹟，賜名治平寶鑑，命諸大臣進講。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered scholars of the Southern and Imperial Studies to compile deeds from earlier histories; they were granted the title Precious Mirror of Ordered Governance, and the grand ministers were ordered to lecture on them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered the Southern and Imperial Studies to compile historical precedents, named the collection Precious Mirror of Ordered Governance, and directed the senior ministers to lecture from it.

sentences.zh: 棠階因講漢文帝卻千里馬事，反复推言人主不宜有所嗜好，以啟窺伺之端。

translations.literal: Tangjie, lecturing on Emperor Wen of Han's refusal of horses from a thousand li, repeatedly urged that the ruler should not harbor partial likes, lest this open a gap for those who spy and scheme.
translations.idiomatic: In lecturing on Emperor Wen of Han's refusal of tribute horses, he urged that the ruler must not indulge private tastes, lest others exploit them.

sentences.zh: 自是每進講必原本經義，極論史事，歸於責難陳善。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he lectured he always grounded himself in classical principle, spoke at length on historical events, and concluded by holding the ruler to account while offering good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every lecture began in the classics, drew lessons from history, and ended in frank admonition.

sentences.zh: 四年，恭親王被劾退出軍機，棠階謂王有定難功，時方多故，不當輕棄親賢，入對，力言王非有心之失。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Prince Gong was impeached and removed from the Grand Council, Tangjie said the prince had merit in settling the crisis and that in troubled times one should not lightly abandon a kinsman and worthy; entering audience, he strongly argued the prince's fault was not deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Prince Gong was impeached and left the Grand Council, Tangjie argued that his service in the crisis merited retention; at audience he insisted the prince's error was not intentional.

sentences.zh: 會惇、醇兩王亦奏言奕訢不可遽罷，乃復命入直。

translations.literal: The Princes of Dun and Chun also memorialized that Yixin should not be abruptly dismissed, and he was again ordered to attend council duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Dun and Chun also pleaded for Yixin, and he was restored to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁戰歿曹州，棠階以朝廷賞多罰少，疆臣每存藐玩，上疏極言其弊，於是有申飭直省督撫之諭。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen fell in battle at Caozhou, Tangjie, because the court rewarded much and punished little and frontier ministers often treated orders with contempt, memorialized at length on these abuses; thereupon came an edict rebuking governors-general and governors of the direct provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengge Rinchen died at Caozhou, Tangjie memorialized that excessive rewards and lax punishments made frontier officials contemptuous of orders; the court then rebuked provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 棠階自入直樞廷，軍書旁午，一事稍有未安，輒憂形於色。

translations.literal: From the time Tangjie entered the Grand Council, military documents poured in from all sides; whenever the slightest matter was unsettled, worry showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the Grand Council, with military papers flooding in, the slightest unsettled matter showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 積勞致疾，十一月，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Weariness from overwork brought on illness; in the eleventh month he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion brought on illness; in the eleventh month he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，遣貝勒載治奠醊，賜金治喪，贈太子太保，諡文清。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; he sent the prince Zaiye to offer libations, bestowed gold for the funeral, posthumously gave him the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted the posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned deeply, sent Prince Zaiye to offer libations, granted funeral funds, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave the posthumous name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 棠階初入翰林，即潛心理學，嘗手鈔湯斌遺書以自勗。

translations.literal: When Tangjie first entered the Hanlin, he devoted himself secretly to Neo-Confucian learning and once copied Tang Bin's posthumous writings by hand to encourage himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his Hanlin career he devoted himself to Neo-Confucianism and copied Tang Bin's writings by hand for self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 會通程、硃、陸、王學說，無所偏主，要以克己復禮、身體實行為歸。

translations.literal: He mastered the teachings of the Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, Lu Xiangshan, and Wang Yangming without partiality, taking self-restraint and returning to ritual and bodily practice in action as his aim.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, Lu Xiangshan, and Wang Yangming without partisan bias, aiming at self-restraint, ritual, and practice in daily life.

sentences.zh: 日記自省，畢生不懈。

translations.literal: He kept a diary for self-examination and never slackened throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a diary of self-examination and never slackened.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，既貴，儉約無改。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor; even after he rose to high rank, he remained frugal and abstemious without change.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor; even in high office he lived as frugally as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「憂患者生之門。

translations.literal: He once said: 'Sorrow and peril are the gate of life.'
translations.idiomatic: He once said, 'Adversity is the gate of life.'

sentences.zh: 吾終身不敢忘忍飢待米時也！

translations.literal: I dare never forget the time when I endured hunger waiting for rice!'
translations.idiomatic: I shall never forget going hungry while waiting for rice to arrive!'

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of quotation.)

sentences.zh: 吳廷棟，字竹如，安徽霍山人。

translations.literal: Wu Tingdong, whose style name was Zhuru, was a native of Huoshan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong, style name Zhuru, was from Huoshan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光五年拔貢，授刑部七品小京官，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he was selected as a tribute student from the provincial school and appointed a seventh-rank junior secretary in the Ministry of Justice; he was promoted in succession to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang (1825) he passed the provincial tribute selection and entered the Ministry of Justice as a junior secretary, rising to director.

sentences.zh: 廷棟少好宋儒之學，入官益植節厲行，蹇蹇自靖。

translations.literal: Tingdong from youth loved Song Neo-Confucian learning; after entering office he all the more planted integrity and disciplined his conduct, steadfast and self-restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved Song Neo-Confucianism; in office he cultivated integrity and stern self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，京察一等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he received the top grade in the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he received top marks in the capital personnel review.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎書元兼崇文門副監督，獲販私釀者三十六人，承審者以漏稅擬滿杖。

translations.literal: At the time Vice President Shuyuan also served as deputy supervisor of the Chongwen Gate and seized thirty-six persons smuggling illicit liquor; those conducting the trial proposed the full bamboo penalty for tax evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice President Shuyuan, also deputy supervisor of the Chongwen Gate, seized thirty-six smugglers of illicit liquor; the examiners proposed the maximum bamboo penalty for tax evasion.

sentences.zh: 已而覆訊得書元家人詐贓狀，部臣據以入奏。

translations.literal: Later, on re-examination, the fact that Shuyuan's family members had extorted bribes was obtained, and the ministry officials memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Re-examination then uncovered extortion by Shuyuan's family, and the ministries memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文宗疑書元孤立，降旨切責，會廷棟召對，上詢是獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong suspected Shuyuan was isolated and issued an edict sharply rebuking him; when Tingdong was summoned for audience, the Emperor inquired about the case.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong suspected Shuyuan was being singled out and rebuked the ministries sharply; when Tingdong was summoned, the Emperor asked about the case.

sentences.zh: 廷棟從容敷奏，且詳陳治道之要，言利之害，君子小人之辨，上首肯，獄竟得解。

translations.literal: Tingdong calmly set forth the facts and in detail stated the essentials of governing the Way, the harm of profit-seeking, and the distinction between gentleman and petty man; the Emperor nodded assent, and the case was finally resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong explained the case calmly, then expounded governance, the dangers of profit-seeking, and the gentleman–petty man distinction; the Emperor approved and the case was closed.

sentences.zh: 因詢廷棟讀何書，廷棟以程、硃對。

translations.literal: The Emperor then asked what books Tingdong read; Tingdong answered the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked what he studied; Tingdong named the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「學程、硃者每多迂拘。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Those who study the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi are often rigid and constrained.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'Students of Cheng and Zhu are often rigid.'

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此不善學之過。

translations.literal: He replied: 'That is the fault of poor learning.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'That comes from poor learning.'

sentences.zh: 程、硃以明德為體，新民為用，天下未有有體而無用者。

translations.literal: The Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi take illustrious virtue as substance and renewing the people as function; in the world there is never substance without function.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Zhu take illustrious virtue as substance and renewing the people as function; nothing has substance without function.

sentences.zh: 皇上讀書窮理，以裕知人之識；

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in reading books and exhausting principle, may enlarge the knowledge by which men are discerned;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reads to exhaust principle, you will enlarge your discernment of men;

sentences.zh: 清心寡欲，以養坐照之明。

translations.literal: purify the heart and lessen desires to nurture the clarity of seated illumination.
translations.idiomatic: purify the heart and lessen desires to nurture clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 寤寐求賢，內外得人，天下何憂不治？

translations.literal: Seek the worthy waking and sleeping, and if within and without you obtain the right men, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed?
translations.idiomatic: Seek the worthy without ceasing; with the right men within and without, how can the realm fail to be governed?

sentences.zh: 」上韙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋出為直隸河間知府。

translations.literal: Shortly he went out as prefect of Hejian in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Hejian in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 粵匪北犯畿輔，廷棟練民兵巡防，民倚以為固。

translations.literal: As Cantonese rebels invaded north into the capital region, Tingdong trained militia for patrol and defense, and the people relied on him as a bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping forces pushed into the capital region, he trained militia for defense and the people relied on him.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士勝保督師至河間，責供張甚急，知縣王灴迫於應付，自刎不殊。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sengge Rinchen arrived at Hejian to supervise the army and demanded supplies with great urgency; Prefect Wang Hong, pressed in meeting the demand, attempted suicide but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sengge Rinchen arrived to command troops and demanded supplies urgently; Prefect Wang Hong, unable to meet them, attempted suicide.

sentences.zh: 廷棟詣大營陳其事，勝保矍然，飭部下聽命。

translations.literal: Tingdong went to the main camp and stated the matter; Sengge Rinchen started awake and ordered his subordinates to obey.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong went to the camp and reported the case; Sengge Rinchen was startled and restrained his men.

sentences.zh: 連擢永定河道、直隸按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to commissioner of the Yongding River and provincial judicial commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Yongding River commissioner and Zhili judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以河間京師門戶，廷棟善守禦，得民心，仍留知府任。

translations.literal: Because Hejian was the gateway to the capital and Tingdong was skilled in defense and had won the people's hearts, he was still kept in the prefect's post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hejian guarded the approach to the capital and Tingdong had won the people's trust, he was kept as prefect.

sentences.zh: 四年，軍事定，乃之按察使任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when military affairs were settled, he then took up the post of judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the fighting ended, he took up the judicial commissionership.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Shandong administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時部臣奏請畿內賦稅兼收大錢鈔票各三成，上下交病，總督譚廷襄不敢言。

translations.literal: At the time ministry officials memorialized that taxes within the capital region should be collected thirty percent each in large cash, banknotes, and standard coin, to the harm of high and low alike; Governor Tan Tingxiang dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries proposed collecting capital-region taxes thirty percent each in large cash, notes, and standard coin, harming all parties; Governor Tan Tingxiang dared not object.

sentences.zh: 會廷棟入覲，面奏：「大錢鈔票實不流通。

translations.literal: When Tingdong came to audience he memorialized in person: 'Large cash and banknotes in fact do not circulate.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said frankly, 'Large cash and notes do not circulate.'

sentences.zh: 立法必先便於民方可行，必先信於民方能久。

translations.literal: In making laws one must first make them convenient for the people before they can be carried out; one must first win the people's trust before they can last.
translations.idiomatic: Laws must first benefit the people to work, and first win trust to endure.

sentences.zh: 今條科太多，朝夕更改，國家先不能自信，何以取信於民？

translations.literal: Today there are too many tax items and changes morning and evening; the state itself cannot first have confidence—how can it win the people's trust?
translations.idiomatic: Too many tax items change too often; if the state lacks confidence, how can the people trust it?

sentences.zh: 」上首肯者再。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded assent twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded twice in agreement.

sentences.zh: 既而廷襄入朝，遂奏罷前議。

translations.literal: When Tingxiang later came to court, he memorialized to repeal the earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Tingxiang came to court, he memorialized to repeal the proposal.

sentences.zh: 山東吏治久窳，廷棟獎廉懲貪。

translations.literal: Shandong administration had long been corrupt; Tingdong rewarded integrity and punished greed.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong government had long been corrupt; Tingdong rewarded the honest and punished the greedy.

sentences.zh: 方議海口立局收貨捐，持不可。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of establishing a bureau at the estuary to collect commodity levies, he held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed a commodity levy bureau at the estuary, he opposed it.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐奏銷遲誤，降補直隸按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for delay in reporting accounts, he was demoted and reassigned as judicial commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was demoted to Zhili judicial commissioner for delayed accounts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復調山東。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he returned to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，入為大理寺卿，尋擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he entered the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review and was soon promoted to vice president of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi he became president of the Court of Judicial Review and soon vice president of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南平，廷棟上疏，略曰：「萬方之治亂在朝政，百工之敬肆視君心。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the south was pacified, Tingdong memorialized in summary: 'Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends on court governance; whether the hundred offices are respectful or lax depends on the ruler's heart.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after the south was pacified, he memorialized: 'Order and disorder depend on the court; official discipline reflects the ruler's heart.'

sentences.zh: 事不貴文，貴其實；

translations.literal: Matters are not prized for ornament but for substance;
translations.idiomatic: What matters is substance, not rhetoric;

sentences.zh: 下不從令，從所好。

translations.literal: subordinates do not follow orders but follow what is favored.
translations.idiomatic: subordinates follow what the ruler favors, not what he commands.

sentences.zh: 夫治亂決於敬肆，敬肆根於喜懼。

translations.literal: Whether there is order or disorder is decided by respect or laxity; respect and laxity root in joy and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder turn on respect or laxity, which root in joy and fear.

sentences.zh: 自古功成志遂，人主喜心一生而驕心已伏，宦寺有乘其喜而貢諂媚者矣，左右有乘其喜而肆蒙蔽者矣，容悅之臣有因此而工諛佞者矣，屏逐之姦有因此而巧夤緣者矣。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when merit is achieved and aims fulfilled, the joy of the ruler is born and the heart of pride is already lurking; eunuchs take advantage of his joy to offer flattery, those at his side take advantage of his joy to indulge in concealment and deception, ministers who please take this occasion to practice adulation and craft, and expelled villains take this occasion to scheme for advancement by crafty connections.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when success is won the ruler's joy breeds pride: eunuchs flatter, attendants deceive, sycophants multiply, and banished schemers claw their way back.

sentences.zh: 諂媚貢則柄暗竊，蒙蔽肆則權下移，諛佞工則主志惑，夤緣巧則宵小升。

translations.literal: When flattery is offered, power is secretly stolen; when concealment runs riot, authority shifts downward; when adulation is practiced, the ruler's will is confused; when crafty connections succeed, petty men rise.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery steals power in secret; deception shifts authority downward; sycophancy confuses the ruler; schemers elevate petty men.

sentences.zh: 於是受蠱惑，塞聰明，遠老成，惡忠鯁。

translations.literal: Thereupon one suffers delusion, blocks clear hearing, distances the mature and worthy, and hates the loyal and blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler is deluded, deafened, estranged from the seasoned, and hostile to the bluntly loyal.

sentences.zh: 從前戒懼之念，一喜敗之；

translations.literal: The former mind of vigilance and fear is ruined by a single joy;
translations.idiomatic: The earlier spirit of vigilance is undone by one burst of joy;

sentences.zh: 此後侈縱之行，一喜開之。

translations.literal: the later conduct of extravagance and license is opened by a single joy.
translations.idiomatic: and the later path of extravagance is opened by that same joy.

sentences.zh: 方且矜予智，樂莫違，逞獨斷，快從欲，一人肆於上，群小扇於下，流毒蒼生，貽禍社稷，稽諸史冊，後先一轍。

translations.literal: One prides oneself on wisdom, delights that none oppose, indulges arbitrary decision, and takes pleasure in following desires; one man is unrestrained above and petty men fan the flames below, poisoning the people and bringing calamity on the altars of state—the historical records, early and late, follow one track.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler trusts his wit, delights in having his way, indulges arbitrary rule and his desires; one man revels above while petty men fan the flames below, poisoning the people and endangering the state—as history shows again and again.

sentences.zh: 推原其端，祗一念由喜入驕而已。

translations.literal: Tracing it to the source, it is only a single thought passing from joy into pride.
translations.idiomatic: The root is a single thought: joy slipping into pride.

sentences.zh: 軍興以來，十數省億萬生靈慘遭鋒鏑，即倡亂之奸民，何一非朝廷赤子？

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, in more than ten provinces hundreds of millions of living beings have suffered cruelly under weapons; even the traitorous commoners who raised rebellion—were they not all the court's own children?
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, tens of millions in a dozen provinces have suffered under arms; even the rebels were once the court's own subjects.

sentences.zh: 大兵所加，盡被誅夷。

translations.literal: Where great armies struck, all were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Where imperial armies marched, all were cut down.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇上體上天好生之心，必有哀矜不忍喜者。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and the Emperor, embodying Heaven's mind to cherish life, must surely have compassion and forbearance and cannot rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and Emperor, embodying Heaven's love of life, must feel compassion, not joy.

sentences.zh: 況旗兵乏食，根本空虛，新疆缺餉，邊陲搖動。

translations.literal: Moreover, banner troops lack food and the root is hollow; Xinjiang lacks pay and the frontier trembles.
translations.idiomatic: Banner troops lack grain, the dynasty's base is hollow, Xinjiang lacks funds, and the frontier is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 兼之強鄰偪處，邪教肆行，豈惟不可喜，而實屬可懼。

translations.literal: In addition, strong neighbors press close and heterodox sects run riot—this is not only not a matter for joy but in truth a matter for fear.
translations.idiomatic: Strong neighbors press close and sectarian movements spread—this is not a time for joy but for fear.

sentences.zh: 假使萬幾之馀，或有一念之肆，臣工效之，視彰癉為故事，輕告戒為具文，積習相沿，工為粉飾，將仍成為叢脞怠荒之局矣。

translations.literal: Suppose that amid the myriad affairs of state there is even a single moment of indulgence—if ministers follow suit, treating reward and punishment as mere routine and light admonitions as empty documents, and if entrenched habits continue with ornament as their craft, the realm will again become a tangle of petty fragments, laxness, and neglect.
translations.idiomatic: If even in a moment of leisure the ruler indulges himself and officials follow, treating discipline as routine and warnings as empty forms, the court will sink again into petty laxity and neglect.

sentences.zh: 是非堅定刻苦，持之以恆，積數十年恭儉憂勤，有未易培國脈復元氣者。

translations.literal: Unless one is firm, painstaking, and holds to this with constancy, accumulating decades of respect, frugality, sorrow, and diligence, it is not easy to strengthen the nation's sinews and restore its vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: Only firm, painstaking constancy over decades of reverence, frugality, and anxious diligence can rebuild the state's strength.

sentences.zh: 夫上行必下效，內治則外安，而其道莫大於敬，其幾必始於懼。

translations.literal: What is done above is necessarily followed below; inner order brings outer peace—and its Way is greatest in respect, and its subtle beginning must lie in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's example shapes all below; inner order secures outer peace—and the greatest principle is reverence, which must begin in fear.

sentences.zh: 懼天命無常，則不敢恃天；

translations.literal: Fearing that Heaven's mandate is inconstant, one dare not rely on Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Heaven's inconstant mandate, one dare not rely on Heaven;

sentences.zh: 懼民碞可畏，則不敢玩民。

translations.literal: fearing that the people's anger is formidable, one dare not trifle with the people.
translations.idiomatic: fearing the people's formidable wrath, one dare not trifle with the people.

sentences.zh: 懼者敬之始，敬者懼之終。

translations.literal: Fear is the beginning of respect; respect is the end of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fear is the beginning of respect; respect is its fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 大智愈明，神武愈彰，紹祖宗富有之大業，開子孫無疆之丕基，是皆由皇心之懼始而敬成也。

translations.literal: Great wisdom grows ever clearer, divine martial prowess ever more manifest; continuing the ancestors' rich enterprise and opening an unbounded foundation for posterity—all this begins in the imperial heart's fear and is completed in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Through fear and respect, wisdom grows, martial glory shines, the ancestors' legacy continues, and the foundation for posterity is laid.

sentences.zh: 易曰：'危者使平，易者使傾，懼以終始，其要無咎。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'What is in peril is made level; what is easy is made to topple—fearing from beginning to end, the essential is to be without blame.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Peril leads to peace, ease to ruin—begin and end in fear, and blame may be avoided.'

sentences.zh: '詩曰：'敬之敬之，天維顯思！

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Revere it, revere it—Heaven clearly sees!'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Revere it, revere it—Heaven clearly sees!'

sentences.zh: '可弗以為永鑑歟？

translations.literal: Can this not be taken as an everlasting mirror?
translations.idiomatic: Can this not serve as an everlasting mirror?

sentences.zh: 」疏上，優詔嘉納，命存其疏於弘​​德殿以備省覽。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial was submitted, an excellent edict graciously accepted it, and he was ordered to keep the memorial in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for reference.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court praised it and ordered it kept in the Hall of Manifest Virtue for reference.

sentences.zh: 皇太后召對時，諭曰：「皇帝衝齡踐阼，國家大事，汝宜直言無隱，以無負先帝知遇。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager summoned him for audience, she instructed: 'The Emperor has taken the throne in his tender years; on great affairs of state you should speak frankly without concealment, lest you fail the late emperor's gracious trust.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience the empress dowager told him: 'The Emperor is young; on great affairs speak frankly and honor the late emperor's trust in you.'

sentences.zh: 」廷棟感激出涕。

translations.literal: Tingdong, moved, shed tears of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，許之，歸寓江寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on grounds of age and illness he begged retirement; this was granted, and he took lodging in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he retired on grounds of age and illness and settled in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，詔褒其廉靜自持，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: When his final memorial was submitted, an edict praised his integrity and quiet self-restraint and granted condolence payments according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial was praised for integrity and quiet self-restraint; condolence followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 直隸、山東皆祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: In Zhili and Shandong he was entered for worship in the shrines of renowned officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili and Shandong enshrined him in their halls of renowned officials.

sentences.zh: 廷棟學以不欺為本。

translations.literal: Tingdong took not deceiving as the root of his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong made honesty the root of his learning.

sentences.zh: 官臬司時，畿輔連有逆倫獄，總督慮一月頻入奏幹上怒，廷棟曰：「此吾儕不能教化之過，待罪不暇，敢欺飾耶？

translations.literal: When he was provincial judicial commissioner, the capital region had successive cases of violation of human relations; the governor feared that frequent memorials within a month would anger the Emperor. Tingdong said: 'This is our failure to teach and transform—there is no time for awaiting punishment; how dare we deceive and cover up?'
translations.idiomatic: As judicial commissioner, when the capital region saw repeated parricide cases, the governor feared frequent memorials would anger the throne. Tingdong said, 'We failed to teach them—how dare we cover it up?'

sentences.zh: 」及去官，僑居清貧，不受餽遺。

translations.literal: ' When he left office he lived in exile in poverty and would not accept gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived in honest poverty and accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 著有拙修集十卷。

translations.literal: He left the Clumsy Cultivation Collection in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Clumsy Cultivation Collection in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：倭仁晚為兩宮所敬禮，際會中興，輔導衝主，兢兢於君心敬肆之間，當時舉朝嚴憚，風氣賴以維持。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Wo Ren in his later years was revered and honored by the two palaces; he met the opportunity of restoration, assisted and guided the young ruler, and was scrupulous in the ruler's heart between respect and laxity; at the time the whole court stood in awe of him, and public morals were thereby sustained.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal: Wo Ren in his later years was honored by the two palaces; at the restoration he tutored the young emperor and guarded the boundary between reverence and laxity in the imperial heart; the whole court stood in awe of him, and public morals were sustained.

sentences.zh: 惟未達世變，於自強要政，鄙夷不屑言，後轉為異論者所藉口。

translations.literal: Only he did not grasp the changes of the age; toward essential policies of self-strengthening he showed contempt and disdained to speak, and this later became a pretext seized upon by those of heterodox views.
translations.idiomatic: His failing was that he did not grasp how the world had changed: he scorned the policies of self-strengthening and refused to discuss them, a stance later seized upon by critics of reform.

sentences.zh: 李棠階、吳廷棟正色立朝，不負所學，翕然笙磬同音，而棠階尤平實持大體，可謂體用兼備矣。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong stood with stern countenance at court, did not betray their learning, and were harmonious as pipes and chimes in unison; yet Tangjie especially was plain and practical and held to the larger pattern—one may say he combined substance and function in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong served at court with unbending integrity true to their learning, moving in concert like matched instruments; Tangjie above all was plain, practical, and steady in grasping the larger pattern—truly a man in whom principle and practice were one.
